annotations.description: Only 2 of 3 brokers are reachable; the cluster tolerates one loss.

diagnosis.summary: Kafka broker lakehouse-dual-role-0 is Running/Ready but network-isolated (Prometheus cannot scrape it, Loki has no logs from it), leaving 60 under-replicated partitions and zero fault-tolerance margin. A Chaos Mesh experiment deployed ~133 min ago (and updated again 15–33 min ago) is the almost-certain cause — do not restart the broker; escalate to stop the chaos experiment.
diagnosis.root_cause: lakehouse-dual-role-0 is Running and Ready per Kubernetes but is completely unreachable at the network level: Prometheus cannot scrape its metrics endpoint (brokers_scraped_up=false), Loki returns no logs, and 60 partitions are under-replicated (its replicas have fallen out of ISR with the other brokers). All three brokers were killed with exit_code=255/Unknown ~129 minutes ago, coinciding with the first chaos-mesh-local deployment ~133 minutes ago. A further chaos-mesh-local revision was pushed ~15–33 minutes ago (around when the alert fired), consistent with a Chaos Mesh NetworkChaos experiment now isolating broker-0 at the pod-network level. active_controllers=0 in scraped metrics further suggests broker-0 holds the KRaft controller role and cannot be reached. The fix is not a broker restart (the network fault is external to the pod; restarting removes ISR evidence without fixing the isolation). The chaos experiment must be stopped.
diagnosis.impact: Kafka is degraded but still serving writes: under_min_isr_partitions=0 and offline_partitions=0, so producers and consumers are unaffected today. However there is zero fault-tolerance — a second broker loss stops all writes. Flink job events-to-iceberg is RUNNING/STABLE with mild consumer lag (200 messages) and completing checkpoints normally (~28/5 min). No data loss has occurred yet.

evidence.finding: All 3 broker pods Running 1/1, but lakehouse-dual-role-0 has brokers_scraped_up=false. under_replicated_partitions=60, under_min_isr_partitions=0, offline_partitions=0, active_controllers=0. All brokers show last_termination reason=Unknown exit_code=255 finished ~129 min ago. Consumer lag flink-events-to-iceberg=200.
All 3 worker nodes Ready, no pressure, spread across zone-a/b/c. No node failure — the problem is not a lost node.

chaos-mesh-local first deployed ~133 min ago (revision 9187ff9e9e6f), then again at ~32.5, ~19.8, and ~15.5 min ago. The broker kill events (~129 min ago) line up with the first chaos-mesh deploy; the most recent chaos-mesh update at ~15–19 min ago coincides with broker-0 becoming network-unreachable.
get_pod_logs for lakehouse-dual-role-0 returned no data — the pod's log stream is unreachable, consistent with network-level isolation, not a crash.
Loki query for {namespace=kafka, pod=lakehouse-dual-role-0} returned no data for the last 30 minutes — no log lines emitted or reachable, reinforcing network isolation.

Runbook docs/runbooks/kafka.md#kafkabrokerdown: 'A broker that is Running and Ready but not reachable … is cut off from the network, not crashed: check NetworkPolicies, the node's network and recent changes (including chaos experiments). Do not restart a broker that is cut off from the network.'
Flink job RUNNING/STABLE, started 127.9 min ago (recovered after the chaos kill). 28.23 completed checkpoints/5 min, 0 failed checkpoints, last checkpoint 1154 ms. Consumer lag 200.

proposed_action.rationale: The root cause is an active Chaos Mesh NetworkChaos experiment isolating broker-0 at the network layer. Restarting the pod would not fix the network isolation and would destroy ISR history as the runbook explicitly warns. Stopping or deleting the Chaos Mesh experiment requires access to the chaos-mesh namespace and a judgement call about whether the chaos run was intentional. A human must inspect and remove the offending ChaosEngine/NetworkChaos CR.

follow_ups: Inspect Chaos Mesh CRs (kubectl get networkchaos,podchaos -A) to identify and delete the experiment targeting lakehouse-dual-role-0.
Confirm whether the chaos experiment was intentional (scheduled test) or accidental; the multiple rapid chaos-mesh-local Argo CD deployments in the last 33 minutes suggest uncontrolled iteration.
Once the experiment is removed, monitor under_replicated_partitions — it should drop to 0 as broker-0 rejoins ISR without any restart.
Check active_controllers after broker-0 is reachable; if it stays 0 the KRaft quorum may need attention.
Consider adding a chaos-mesh experiment approval gate or time-window guard to prevent production Kafka disruption during business hours.
The log line 'do not restart' guidance in the runbook should be surfaced directly in the alert annotation to prevent well-meaning responders from deleting the pod.
